scope: The surviving Busch Stadium opened in 2006, with the red-brick gate elevations, three-tier seating bowl, open northeast view, baseball diamond, two current-generation outfield board housings, canopy and lighting structures.
geometryBasis: The named stadium multipolygon supplies 145 outer and 55 inner controls. Native playing-surface relations locate the turf and warning track, and six mapped gate nodes anchor exterior openings.
sectionBasis: Tall red seating decks and a narrow dark canopy surround the first-base, third-base and behind-home-plate stands. The deck drops toward the open northeast outfield with red-brick gates, field-level bleachers and two large video boards.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: Design/build engineers document the cast concrete and steel grandstands, steel entrance arch inspired by Eads Bridge, and open center field.
Cardinals stadium records supply the 336, 400 and 335 foot foul-line and center-field dimensions and the eight-foot outfield wall.
The Cardinals document the two LED screens fitted in 2016 and their 120-by-40 and 81-by-40 foot dimensions.
The Cardinals identify the west approach at Gate 3, east Broadway entry and center-field Ford Plaza.

next: Build the asymmetric three-deck seating bowl, brick entries, narrow canopy, two LED boards, and light standards. Check the warning track against the original terrain.

playingField.controls: Exact mapped grass, clay, warning track and mound rings. Foul lines and bases inferred from the mapped turf and regulation baseball geometry.
playingField.originalFieldNote: The green field boundary sits below the modeled surface. Some original elevations are higher along the mapped outer warning track.
